rationale: The assistant immediately reassured without over-promising, then asked the exact sensible first checks (flat/dry base, try a different pan at high power), and correctly concluded from the pan-dependent, power-dependent evidence that this is normal induction noise, matching the hidden truth. No parts, no fabricated evidence, and the burning/tripping safety panel covers the relevant stop condition. Minor weaknesses: one garbled sentence ('Burning smells, or cracking sounds, your hob is fine.') and no explicit statement of when to book an engineer (e.g. noise with all pans, codes, harsh rattling), though the generic safety panel partly covers this.
